# Synthetic Report 9001 — Two-Stage Normalisation Pipeline

This report is a **test fixture**, not a scientific result. It exists so the three
gates of the production line can be exercised offline with a source whose bytes
are pinned and whose claims are checkable character by character.

## 1 Purpose

The report describes a two-stage pipeline that normalises inputs before aggregation.
The question it answers is whether normalising before aggregation changes the spread
of the aggregated output.

## 2 Method

Stage one applies a fixed window of 7 samples and reports the median of the window.
Stage two aggregates the medians with equal weights and a tolerance of 0.5 percent.

The pipeline assumes that consecutive samples are independent. This assumption is not
tested in the report.

## 3 Results

The pipeline reduced variance by 41.2 percent on the bundled sample set.
The reduction was measured against the same inputs aggregated without normalisation.

## 4 Limitations

The bundled sample set holds 24 records, so the variance reduction is established for
that set only and must not be extrapolated to other inputs.
No experiment was run on a second data set.

## 5 Conclusion

Normalising before aggregation is a defensible default for data sets of the shape used
here, provided the independence assumption in section 2 is acceptable.
